Subject: Re: Redshifts shifted after upgrade to lumenfit 2.5.0?

I did read the changelog, and I read it again after your reply. It says "Refactor LineList and spectral frame handling (#812)." That does not tell a user that the default spectral frame changed. I found the actual cause today in the PR #812 diff: `LineList.__init__` changed the default `wave_frame` from `'air'` to `'vacuum'`. For air-calibrated optical spectra, that produces a shift of about 1.00028 in wavelength, i.e. ~83 km/s at H-alpha. That is exactly the offset I reported.

This was not a calibration or config problem on my end. I spent two days re-reducing arc lamps for 40 spectra chasing a mistake that wasn't there. m_okonkwo also reports a small offset in the same thread, so this is not just me.

"Works for me" is not a test here. If your data are already in vacuum wavelengths, or are radio data where the air/vacuum distinction doesn't apply, you would see no difference at all. That doesn't mean the default didn't change for everyone else.

Workaround for anyone finding this thread: for air-calibrated spectra, construct the line list explicitly with `LineList(..., wave_frame='air')`. That restores the 2.4.x behavior.

Please reopen this thread. The fix on the project side should be either a line in CHANGES that says the default `wave_frame` changed, or a warning when `wave_frame` is not set explicitly. "Refactor" is not enough for a silent default change that shifts every redshift. This is a library-level default change, not user error, and a changelog line or warning would have saved me—and likely others—two days.
